question: Does the machine's native Iota/S/K substrate reproduce the recorded behavioural contract of the external iota-lang checkout, case by case, when each case is transcribed faithfully rather than re-encoded?
level: Research-local native Rust reduction over a recorded external test contract. No ValueType, OperationSpec, registry entry, IR version, Seal or stable semantic type is added; the iota-lang checkout is read, never modified or imported.
assumptions: The recorded contract is src/tests/java/iota/SKITest.java at checkout HEAD a1865e6d70d55a0d9457b33570e533463818d7d6, sha256 c9b84b9206daa10c5977e22f90bc30ba9cbe016c038ad1036644d8025a58e133, 17 @Test methods.
In the case grammar the token i is the identity combinator, k is K, s is S and the Iota combinator is written ι or j; lowercase words are opaque variables.
In the murphy grammar the character i is the Iota combinator. The two grammars are separate declarations and no term mixes them.
The rules are the declared Iota/S/K rules: j a -> a S K, I a -> a, K a b -> a, S x y z -> x z (y z).
Reduction order is leftmost-outermost, with one contraction counted per applied combinator.
Every expectation is transcribed from the recorded file unchanged; a case whose expectation the declared rules do not reach is retained as a mismatch rather than repaired.
The iota-lang sources never compiled and its machine was never executed (Research 0167), so the recorded expectations are a written contract, not a recording of a running machine.

cases.label: testXY
cases.note: A form whose head is an opaque variable: no redex exists.

cases.label: testI
cases.note: The identity combinator in the case grammar.

cases.label: testFalse
cases.note: S applied to a raw combinator: S K x y = K y (x y) = y under the declared arity rules.

cases.label: testReverse
cases.note: The recorded reverse form; (s i) is a partial application and stays.

cases.label: testKSKS
cases.note: K with two combinators as operands.

cases.label: testKKKSKS
cases.note: A deeper operand-nesting case of the same kind.

cases.label: testSKK
cases.note: S K K behaves as the identity on two opaque variables.

cases.label: testIIII
cases.note: Four identities; the recorded file builds this term, not a repeated (i i).

cases.label: testIota2
cases.note: The Iota encoding of the identity combinator.

cases.label: testIota4
cases.note: The Iota encoding of K: 3 iotas nested, matching the resource definitions under a right-nested list reading.

cases.label: testIota5
cases.note: The Iota encoding of S: 4 iotas nested.

comparison.note: The audit's replay of the same 17 cases against the reconnected Java machine, supplied independently and used only to compare transcriptions: for each case this run reports whether the transcript's term is the recorded term. The transcript is never used as an expected value.

acceptance: Every case must reduce inside the declared bounds and print exactly the recorded expectation. A case that does not is retained as a mismatch and fails the run. The transcription comparison is reported separately and does not change any verdict.
residual: This is a case corpus, not a language equivalence. It does not establish that the recorded iota-lang machine agrees with this substrate, that the substrate implements the SKI or Iota calculus, or that the recorded expectations are the intended semantics of iota-lang: the checkout never compiled, its machine was never executed, and its test file declares none of the identifiers it uses. The parser cases, the DualMachine suite and the two Clojure-shaped resource definitions are outside this contract and are not executed here. Native admission remains NotGranted.
